text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm sketching a follow-up to the onboarding RFC focusing on where to run lightweight preflight vs full bench. Need a quick sync.
aj: Do we have current run-time numbers for the bench suites vs smoke? ballpark mins/hours?
cheng: Full microbench suite on 8 configs is ~45m-1h; smoke (sanity + small perf probes) is ~2-3m. Numbers vary by model size.
liz: My proposal: run the smoke in the intake layer (fast ephemeral container) and run the full bench in the benchhouse (scheduled or on-demand). Smoke should produce a clear pass/investigate binary.
noah: How strict should smoke be? false positives will block a lot of intake. I argue for graded gates: smoke (syntactic + tiny perf), profile (kv/cache correctness), final full bench.
maria: Agree on tiers. Also we need a canonical artifact layout: single tarball with metadata.json + signature. Metadata should include model_arch, quantized_ops, expected_seq_length_distribution, golden_inputs_sha256. Example metadata.json snippet: ```{
  "schema": "onboard-manifest.v1",
  "model_id": "bertha-v2",
  "arch": "transformer",
  "quantized": "int8",
  "expected_seq_lengths": [64,256,1024],
  "golden_inputs_sha256": "abc123..."
}```
cheng: Important: runtime picks optimized kernels. Record build_id/kernel_versions in metadata so benchhouse/runtime can check kernel_compat. Add a kernel_compat list to the manifest.
aj: Operational question — where exactly should smoke run? intake ephemeral infra or a lightweight runtime sandbox? I prefer intake for speed.
liz: Intake is faster, but KV/cache interactions are runtime-specific. I suggest running basic smoke in intake and a short kv-check in a tiny runtime sandbox (single GPU) as part of smoke.
onboard-bot: bench-queue: smoke/172 queued for model/bertha-v2 on gpu-a1
noah: For metrics, smoke should check tokens/s delta > -10% and logprob diff < 0.5 on the golden set. If it fails, mark as 'investigate' for the first two pushes (don't reject immediately).
maria: API boundaries need to be explicit: intake -> bench orchestrator POST /onboard { artifact_url, metadata_sha, requested_checks } -> returns 202 + check_ids. Example: ```curl -X POST https://bench.internal/onboard -d '{"artifact_url":"s3://...","metadata_sha":"sha256...","requested_checks":["smoke","kv-check"]}'```
cheng: Bench results should be stored reproducibly: bench-result.json, flamegraph.tar.gz, sample-outputs.jsonl, all tagged with manifest_sha and build_id.
liz: Edge case: quantized binaries often pass short-smoke but fail for long-context KV stepping. Add a cheap 'long_context_smoke' that steps 512->2048 tokens with low sample count but exercises KV stepping.
aj: Proposed workflow: intake posts artifact -> smoke runs -> on smoke pass, canary deploy to dedicated pool (low traffic) -> full bench scheduled nightly and available on-demand. Sounds ok?
maria: Decision notes: use canonical RNG seeds for smoke (deterministic prompts) to reduce flakiness. Store seeds in bench-result.json.
noah: Who owns flaky investigations? For now assign to model-owner (team) + ops on-call. Auto-tag a ticket if a model fails >=3 times within 24h.
liz: :thumbsup: I'll draft a PR for intake API + manifest schema and include a small set of test vectors.
maria: Thanks — plan: liz to PR, cheng to add kernel_compat field, aj to update orchestration docs. I'll schedule a 30m review tomorrow 10:00am. @cheng @aj @liz
